Theme

Latin word

perpetuus

perpetuus, perpetua, perpetuum

adjective, declension

unbroken, continuous; permanent, lasting, unbroken

In this lexicon

  • constant

    also used · classical · Traupman 296: constant (incessant), perpetuus; constantly, perpetuō; Traupman 296

  • permanent

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Brut. 105: quaestiōnēs perpetuae, standing courts (Lewis & Short: “a permanent tribunal”); Ov. Tr. 3.10.14: perpetuamque facit

Examples

  • nix jacet, et jactam nē sōl pluviaeque resolvant, indūrat Boreās perpetuamque facit

    snow lies, and once it has fallen, so that neither sun nor rain may melt it, the north wind hardens it and makes it permanentOv. Tr. 3.10.13–14

  • effinge aliquid et excūde, quod sit perpetuō tuum

    shape and hammer out something that will be yours for goodPlin. Ep. 1.3.4
